subject: history
title: Medieval & Early Modern Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the key words and events from 1066 to 1750 — kings, peasants, plague and reform.
meta_desc: GCSE History Medieval & Early Modern foundations — Norman Conquest, feudalism, Black Death, Magna Carta and the Reformation.
final_note: You learned the core vocabulary and big events of medieval and early modern England.

concepts.def: Land in return for loyalty and military service
1086 survey of English land ordered by William I
1348-49 plague that killed about a third of England
Rule by a king or queen with inherited power

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1066 William of Normandy defeated King Harold at the Battle of Hastings.

William built castles, brought French-speaking lords and set up the feudal system — land in exchange for loyalty and soldiers.

In 1215 rebel barons forced King John to seal Magna Carta — the king must obey the law.

In 1348-49 the Black Death killed roughly a third of England. Fewer workers meant peasants could demand better pay.

Henry VIII broke from Rome in the 1530s — the start of the English Reformation.

By 1649 Parliament executed Charles I in the English Civil War. England briefly became a republic under Oliver Cromwell.

free_texts.hint: It's named because its judgements were considered final, like Judgement Day.
